Title: Unemployment Insurance Program National Minimum Weekly Work Search Requirements
Action: Proposed rule, request for comment.
Abstract: The U.S. Department of Labor (Department), through the Employment and Training Administration (ETA), is proposing to amend 20 CFR part 604 both to reflect a 2012 update in Federal law in which Congress, by amending section 303(a) of the Social Security Act (SSA), established a Federal work search requirement; and to establish a national minimum weekly work search requirement standard for the Federal-State unemployment compensation (UC) program. This proposed rule would mandate, among other things, that States require individuals claiming UC to complete at least five qualifying work search activities or, where applicable, meet State-adopted points-based system requirements amounting to five qualifying activities or satisfy equivalent labor force attachment criteria, each week for which UC is claimed; that individuals report their work search activities as part of their certification process prior to payment being issued; and that State law allow for certain qualifying work search activities beyond simply employer contacts.
